title: Finding sangat
hookLine: look for people who help you remember
tomorrow: she checks the map. nearest gurdwara: two hours away. now what?

cards: The club fair on the college tour is loud. A drumline. A dance crew blasting music from a speaker.
A table handing out free pizza to anyone who signs a clipboard. Simran walks the whole quad with Harjit, and every table wants her. Hiking club, debate, robotics.
On the drive back she's quiet for an hour, then says: everybody wanted me to join something. Nobody there would help me remember. Harjit keeps his eyes on the road.
So how do you find the ones who would?

teach.b: Sangat means company, and in Sikh life it means the congregation, the people you sit with before the Guru. Guru Nanak asks the very question Simran asked, on Ang 72. In paraphrase: how is the true company known?

teach.h: ANG 72: WHERE THE ONE NAME IS SPOKEN.
teach.b: It's where the one Name is spoken. That's the test. Not the same turban, not the same hometown, not even the same playlist.
The sangat you're looking for is the company that turns you back toward the One, the people who leave you a little more yourself and a little less scattered.
Listen for it, almost literally. In a gurdwara you can hear it before you see it: the harmonium, a room singing the same line back, the hush when the Hukamnama is read.
Off campus or on, it might sound like a friend who asks how your Japji's going, or one who just goes quiet with you before a test. In Sikh life, the company you keep is taken seriously.
Simran doesn't find her people that day. But she's learned what she's listening for. The quad was loud.
The test is whether the one Name can be heard in it.

how: Sikhs find sangat at the gurdwara, at kirtan and study circles, at Sikh student associations on some campuses, and in small groups that meet at home to read and sing Gurbani.

o: moving close to the biggest gurdwara you can
joining whichever group invites you first
looking for the company that helps you remember

p: true company: where the Name is spoken
do they turn you back toward the One?

s: a true sangat has to share your background or hometown
Ang 72's test is where the one Name is spoken, not who looks like you.
Guru Nanak asks how the true company is known
Ang 72: it's known where the one Name is spoken.
any group that wants you is your sangat
every table wanted Simran; the test is whether they help you remember.

games.q: first week at a new school. a group invites you every night; you have fun, but you feel scattered after. another kid asks if you want to study together quietly. going by Ang 72, what do you weigh?
o: which company turns you back toward what matters, not just which is fun.
whichever group is bigger, because more people means more support.
neither: sangat only happens inside a gurdwara.
games.why: Guru Nanak's test on Ang 72 isn't size or fun: it's whether the one Name is spoken there, whether it leaves you more yourself.

practice: Think of one person who helps you remember what matters to you. Say their name out loud, softly, once, and listen to how it sounds in the room.
Then sit with that sound for the rest of the time, and if you pray, you can say Waheguru after it, quietly, between breaths.

wordCard.voice: Finding sangat. Looking for the company where the one Name is spoken: the people who help you remember.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: satsangat, true company, the word Guru Nanak uses on Ang 72.

carryVoice: Something to keep: find your people, the ones who turn you back toward the One. That's today.

sources.ref: Ang 72, Sri Raag, Guru Nanak (satsangat kaisee jaaneeai, jithai eko naam vakhaaneeai), paraphrased
